title: API Testing Is More Than Checking Responses
excerpt: A green response doesn't mean the system behaved correctly. Real API testing means validating data, logic, and consistency, not just status codes.
html:
API testing is often misunderstood as simply sending requests and checking responses. In reality, that is only a small part of the process.

A successful HTTP response does not guarantee correct system behavior. True API testing focuses on validation: ensuring data integrity, verifying business logic, and confirming system consistency across workflows.

This is where Postman becomes more powerful than just an API client. Pre-request scripts help create dynamic test data instead of relying on static inputs, and post-request tests help verify responses and catch issues early.

Environment variables also make a big difference by keeping test flows clean, reusable, and easy to maintain.

In the end, API testing is not about sending requests. It is about verifying what those requests actually do.
